title: UK labour market overview — earnings, unemployment and vacancies (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the first labour print AFTER the February forecast round rather than before it
source: EST: gov.uk/government/statistics/announcements/uk-labour-market-february-2027, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the statutory pre-announcement register reads 'UK Labour Market February 2027', '16 February 2027 at 7:00am (confirmed)', producer Office for National Statistics, designation 'Accredited official statistics', contents 'employment, unemployment, inactivity, average weekly earnings, vacancies and related labour market data for the UK'. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap all five 2026-27 siblings were filed under. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-labour-market-2027-01-19, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-labour-market-2027-01-19 LANE, 2026-09-09. WHY IT EARNS A SLOT: it is the load-bearing negative in the proposing lane's placement claim, so filing it means no later lane has to re-derive it. uk-labour-market-2027-01-19 asserts it is the LAST labour read before the 2027-02-04 Monetary Policy Report round; that assertion is only true because THIS print falls twelve days after that round rather than before it. The date is a fetched register entry, not an inferred third-Tuesday guess. WHAT IT CARRIES, by the window rule the chain has reconfirmed across four bulletins (headline AWE/LFS = the three months ending two months before the release month; vacancies end one month before; the payrolled-employees flash is the month before): OCT-DEC 2026 average weekly earnings and Labour Force Survey estimates, NOV 2026-JAN 2027 vacancies, JANUARY 2027 payroll flash. NOTE WHAT THAT SETTLES, because two documents in this chain got it wrong: Oct-Dec is NOT the first wholly post-Budget AWE window — 27 of October's 31 days precede the 2026-10-28 Budget. The proposal that created uk-labour-market-2027-01-19 and the uk-labour-market-2026-12-15 ledger's leg 8 both name 'the FEBRUARY 2027 release' as the first wholly post-Budget one; it is the MARCH 2027 release (Nov 2026-Jan 2027), dated 16 March 2027 on the same register. TIERED LOW on the same argued grounds as every sibling: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol, no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed, and the measured cable reaction to the 2026-08-18 release was ~0.1% on a two-sided beat. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
